answer: A walnut buyers guild near a glacier treats each trusted sponsor as a source of ten admission credits. Delegation moves credits; it never creates them, and the ledger rejects reuse, including cycles through aliases. A relic of ten old keys therefore cannot become a thousand funded seats. Extra access requires convincing additional independent sponsors to spend their limited budgets, displacing real customers. This assumes trustworthy initial sponsors and conserved credits across the whole graph; fake roots or bribed sponsors can still admit a farm.
